title: adversarial-review ledger event record
description: One thing that happened to a finding. Events are the only way a finding's state changes, which is what keeps the ledger append-only in fact and not just in spirit. Every key is present on every event and inapplicable ones are null — a fabricated value in an evidence field would be indistinguishable from a real one later. Cross-field rules (REPRODUCED needs its command and output, NOT_REPRODUCED needs counter-evidence) live in ledger.py, since the conservative keyword set cannot express them.

disposition.description: The first three are verification outcomes and only REPRODUCED can block. The rest record what was then done about it.

actor.description: Who produced this event, e.g. verifier-r1-money. A verification event whose actor is the finder is the failure this whole gate exists to prevent.

repro_command.description: The command actually run, which may differ from the proposed one.

observed_output.description: What the command actually printed. Required on REPRODUCED: an unreproduced finding with a confident summary attached is exactly the artifact this design refuses to produce.

counter_evidence.description: Required on NOT_REPRODUCED. Closing a finding is a claim too, and it carries the same evidence bar.

reason.description: Required on UNVERIFIABLE. Says why the check could not run — an unsafe repro command, a missing fixture, an environment the verifier cannot reach.

artifact.description: The thing produced: a failing test's path, an issue URL, a filed question's path.
